Subject: Re: Production slowdown: sustained 500s/latency spike since 09:00 PT

Quick summary from infra: we see a sudden spike in token issuance from ACME's tenant that coincides with a large number of retries from their side. Our tenant-level burst allocation (token-bucket) depleted and the configured burst refill rate is lower than expected for the current traffic shape. That caused per-tenant short-term hard throttles; retries amplified the problem and led to queue congestion upstream which manifested as 5xx on the customer side.

Immediate actions taken (completed within 15m):
- Temporarily increased per-tenant burst allowance for ACME's dedicated pool (bypass flag) to smooth the token flow.
- Enabled emergency per-tenant queue drain policy for their pool to prevent head-of-line blocking.
- Instrumented additional tracing on token-bucket consumption to validate refill behavior.

We have a more durable fix options list: raise default burst tokens for Dedicated customers with high tail variance; add dynamic burst scaling when retry rates exceed threshold; and patch a misinterpretation in our config parser that caused a factor-of-10 lower refill for this pool after last week's policy sync.

I’m preparing a short exec brief and remediation timeline now. Attaching runbook we used.

— Marcus

Subject: Exec brief: ACME Prod — token-burst policy misalignment caused production throttling (summary + asks)

Team — short executive summary and asks (for leadership attention):

What happened:
- 09:00 PT: ACME experienced a marked increase in request rate and retries during a client-side maintenance job.
- Our per-tenant burst token bucket for their Dedicated pool depleted faster than expected due to a config parser discrepancy introduced in last week's policy sync. That produced short-term hard throttles and upstream queue congestion, resulting in elevated 5xx and reduced throughput for ACME.

Impact:
- Customer-facing degradation for ~45 minutes, throughput nadir ~40% of baseline, ~3–5% residual 429s during heavy windows.
- Customer release scheduled for 14:00 PT was at risk; ACME's leadership is requesting an exec call and potential credits for the impact window.

Remediation completed / in-progress:
- Emergency increase to per-tenant burst allowance applied (completed).
- Queue drain policy applied to their pool (completed).
- Config parser bug fix identified; patch in staging, deployment scheduled after validation (ETA 24–48h).
- Post-incident post-mortem and quota policy review scheduled — recommended to add dynamic burst scaling for Dedicated tenants.

Asks for leadership:
1) Approve a one-time goodwill credit (range: 5–10% of the impacted usage bill) contingent on PM/Finance input.
2) Support fast-track approval for the parser patch and a controlled deploy outside peak hours.
3) Decide whether to proactively brief ACME execs or defer to the customer account team for an initial call (I recommend a short joint call with Neha + Marcus + one exec).

Attachments: incident logs and temporary runbook used for bypass. I’ll schedule a 30-min exec update if leadership agrees.

— Tessa
